## Project Overview

This notebook prepares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** program data for analysis and reporting. It ingests two raw exports from the eInsight clinical management platform, cleans and recodes each, joins them together, and writes clean CSVs used by downstream analysis scripts.

**Data sources (eInsight exports):**

- **Discharge Report** — One row per client assessment pair (pre/post). Contains intervention dates, pre/post measure names, and funding round.
- **Client Demographics** — One row per client (ideally). Contains race, ethnicity, language, age, provider, and other client characteristics.

**Outputs:**

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `demographic_data_clean.csv` | Deduplicated, recoded demographic data |
| `discharge_data_clean.csv` | Cleaned discharge/assessment data |
| `demographic_discharge_clean.csv` | Joined dataset for outcome analyses |
| `demographic_duplicate_list.csv` | All rows for client IDs that appear more than once in demographics (for manual review) |

**Demo filter:** rows whose `provider_id` or `client_system_id` contains "DEMO" are removed. Rows with a missing `client_system_id` are removed (they cannot be linked). Rows with a missing `provider_id` are **kept** and counted (previously both were dropped silently by the filter).

# Helper Functions

```{r helpers}
# Converts an ID column to character without scientific notation
# (as.character(100000) gives "1e+05", which breaks joins) and trims whitespace.
id_to_chr <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) if_else(is.na(x), NA_character_, sprintf("%.0f", x)) else str_squish(as.character(x))
}

# Converts an eInsight/Excel date column to Date. Handles columns that arrive as
# Date/POSIXct, as Excel serial numbers, or as a character mix of serials and
# text dates (m/d/y or y-m-d). Years below 100 (e.g., 0025) are shifted by 2000.
# Warns with a count of non-blank values that could not be parsed.
parse_excel_date <- function(x, label) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date"))   return(x)
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) return(as.Date(x))
  if (is.numeric(x))         return(janitor::excel_numeric_to_date(floor(x)))

  x   <- str_squish(as.character(x))
  out <- as.Date(rep(NA_character_, length(x)))

  is_serial <- !is.na(x) & str_detect(x, "^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$")
  if (any(is_serial)) {
    out[is_serial] <- janitor::excel_numeric_to_date(floor(as.numeric(x[is_serial])))
  }
  is_text <- !is.na(x) & !is_serial
  if (any(is_text)) {
    out[is_text] <- as.Date(parse_date_time(x[is_text], orders = c("mdy", "Ymd"), quiet = TRUE))
  }

  # Fix 2-digit years parsed as e.g. year 25 instead of 2025
  fix <- !is.na(out) & year(out) < 100
  out[fix] <- out[fix] + years(2000)

  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Removes demo/test rows (provider_id or client_system_id contains "DEMO") and
# rows with no client_system_id (they cannot be linked or paired). Rows with a
# missing provider_id are kept. Prints a count for each.
remove_demo_rows <- function(df, label) {
  missing_ids <- setdiff(c("provider_id", "client_system_id"), names(df))
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop(label, ": column(s) needed for the demo filter not found: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_demo   <- coalesce(str_detect(df$provider_id, "DEMO"), FALSE) |
               coalesce(str_detect(df$client_system_id, "DEMO"), FALSE)
  no_client <- is.na(df$client_system_id) & !is_demo
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with no client_system_id removed:", sum(no_client),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id) & !is_demo & !no_client), "\n")
  df[!is_demo & !no_client, ]
}

# Splits a comma-separated multi-select field, trims each value, drops
# non-informative responses and blanks, removes repeats, and rejoins with ", ".
# Returns NA when nothing informative remains.
nonresponse_pattern <- "^(don['\u2019]?t know|prefer not to answer|not applicable)$"

clean_multiselect <- function(x, drop = nonresponse_pattern) {
  map_chr(str_split(x, ","), function(values) {
    values <- str_squish(values)
    values <- values[!is.na(values) & values != "" & !str_detect(str_to_lower(values), drop)]
    values <- unique(values)
    if (length(values) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(values, collapse = ", ")
  })
}

# Standardizes extracted time points to "Initial" / "Follow Up N".
standardize_time_point <- function(tp) {
  tp <- str_to_lower(str_squish(tp))
  case_when(
    is.na(tp)       ~ NA_character_,
    tp == "initial" ~ "Initial",
    TRUE            ~ paste("Follow Up", str_extract(tp, "\\d+"))
  )
}
```

# 1. Read in Raw Data

Both files are pulled from the eInsight export folder in the shared Dropbox. The `na` argument ensures that common "missing" strings are treated as `NA` from the start. Column names are cleaned to snake_case via `janitor::clean_names()`, and ID columns are converted to text so they compare and join consistently. The pre/post completion dates can arrive as Excel serial numbers, text dates, or a mix, and are converted with the same helper.

```{r read-data}
discharge_data <- read_xlsx(discharge_path, na = na_vals) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(across(any_of(id_cols), id_to_chr))

discharge_data <- discharge_data |>
  mutate(
    pre_completion_date  = parse_excel_date(pre_completion_date,  "pre_completion_date"),
    post_completion_date = parse_excel_date(post_completion_date, "post_completion_date")
  )

demographic_data <- read_xlsx(demographic_path, na = na_vals) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(across(any_of(id_cols), id_to_chr))

# Quick row/ID counts
cat("Discharge rows:          ", nrow(discharge_data), "\n")
cat("Demographic rows:        ", nrow(demographic_data), "\n")
cat("Unique demographic IDs:  ", n_distinct(demographic_data$client_system_id), "\n")
```

# 2. Clean Demographic Data

## 2.1 Remove Demo/Test Accounts

eInsight includes test provider and client accounts with "DEMO" in their IDs. These are not real clients and must be excluded before any analysis.

```{r demo-filter-demographics}
demographic_data_filtered <- remove_demo_rows(demographic_data, "Demographics")

# Possible test accounts not caught by the "DEMO" rule (review; not removed)
demographic_data_filtered |>
  filter(if_any(c(provider_id, client_system_id),
                ~ str_detect(.x, regex("demo|test", ignore_case = TRUE)))) |>
  count(provider_id, name = "n_rows")
```

## 2.2 Identify and Handle Duplicate Client IDs

The demographics export should have one row per client, but some clients appear more than once (e.g., due to selecting multiple languages or data entry errors). We identify duplicates, export them for review, then drop them from the analysis dataset for now.

```{r demo-duplicates}
# Identify which client IDs appear more than once
duplicates <- demographic_data_filtered |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  tally()

cat("Client IDs with duplicates:", nrow(duplicates), "\n")
cat("Total duplicated rows:     ", sum(duplicates$n), "\n")

# Inspect which columns differ across duplicate rows for the same client
demographic_data_filtered |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  summarise(
    across(everything(), ~ {
      u <- unique(.x)
      if (length(u) > 1) paste(u, collapse = ", ") else NA_character_
    }),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  select(client_system_id, where(~ any(!is.na(.))))
```

```{r demo-save-duplicates}
# Export the full duplicate records for manual review
duplicate_list <- demographic_data_filtered |>
  filter(client_system_id %in% duplicates$client_system_id)

write_csv(duplicate_list, file.path(out_dir, "demographic_duplicate_list.csv"))
```

```{r demo-drop-duplicates}
# Drop all rows for clients with any duplicate — conservative approach until
# a resolution strategy is decided for these records
demographic_data_filtered <- demographic_data_filtered |>
  filter(!(client_system_id %in% duplicates$client_system_id))

# Confirm one row per client (stops the render if not)
stopifnot(n_distinct(demographic_data_filtered$client_system_id) == nrow(demographic_data_filtered))
```

## 2.3 Recode Race

Race is stored as a free-text, comma-separated field. We clean it in two passes:

1. Split on commas, trim each value, and drop non-informative responses ("Don't Know", "Prefer Not To Answer", "Not Applicable"; matched case-insensitively, including curly apostrophes) and repeats. Remaining values are rejoined with ", ".
2. Recode to a numeric summary:
   - `NA` — no valid response after stripping
   - `1` — exactly one valid race reported
   - `2` — two or more valid races reported (multiracial)
   - `code_num` assigns each single-race response a numeric code, or `88` for multiracial.

Splitting value by value fixes cases where leftover separators were misread: previously "White, Don't Know" could be left as "White, " and coded multiracial, and "Don't Know, White" could be left as " White" and receive no code.

```{r recode-race}
codebook_race <- c(
  "Asian"                                                = 1,
  "Black or African American"                            = 2,
  "Hispanic or Latino"                                   = 3,
  "Middle Eastern or North African"                      = 4,
  "Native American/American Indian or Alaska Native"     = 5,
  "Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander"                  = 6,
  "White"                                                = 7
)

demographic_data_filtered <- demographic_data_filtered |>
  mutate(cleaned_race = clean_multiselect(race)) |>
  mutate(
    recoded_race = case_when(
      is.na(cleaned_race)              ~ NA,   # no valid response
      str_detect(cleaned_race, ",")    ~ 2L,   # multiracial
      TRUE                             ~ 1L    # single race
    ),
    code_num = case_when(
      is.na(cleaned_race)              ~ NA,
      str_detect(cleaned_race, ",")    ~ 88L,  # multiracial code
      TRUE ~ unname(codebook_race[cleaned_race])
    )
  )

# Single-race values with no codebook entry (these get code_num = NA)
demographic_data_filtered |>
  filter(recoded_race == 1, is.na(code_num)) |>
  count(cleaned_race, name = "n_clients", sort = TRUE)
```

## 2.4 Recode Ethnicity

Same two-pass approach as race. Ethnicity is also stored as a comma-separated string. Non-informative values are removed and responses are recoded to numeric codes; `88` = 2+ ethnicities selected.

```{r recode-ethnicity}
codebook_eth <- c(
  "Chinese" = 1, "Asian Indian" = 2, "Filipino" = 3, "Vietnamese" = 4,
  "Korean" = 5, "Japanese" = 6, "African American" = 7, "Jamaican" = 8,
  "Haitian" = 9, "Nigerian" = 10, "Somali" = 11, "Mexican" = 12,
  "Puerto Rican" = 13, "Salvadoran" = 14, "Cuban" = 15, "Dominican" = 16,
  "Guatemalan" = 17, "Native Hawaiian" = 18, "Samoan" = 19, "Chamorro" = 20,
  "English" = 21, "German" = 22, "Irish" = 23, "Italian" = 24, "Polish" = 25,
  "Scottish" = 26, "2+ ethnicities selected" = 88
)

demographic_data_filtered <- demographic_data_filtered |>
  mutate(cleaned_ethn = clean_multiselect(ethnicity)) |>
  mutate(
    recoded_ethn = case_when(
      is.na(cleaned_ethn)              ~ NA,
      str_detect(cleaned_ethn, ",")    ~ 2L,
      TRUE                             ~ 1L
    ),
    ethn_num = case_when(
      is.na(cleaned_ethn)              ~ NA,
      str_detect(cleaned_ethn, ",")    ~ 88L,
      TRUE ~ unname(codebook_eth[cleaned_ethn])
    )
  )

# Single-ethnicity values with no codebook entry (these get ethn_num = NA)
demographic_data_filtered |>
  filter(recoded_ethn == 1, is.na(ethn_num)) |>
  count(cleaned_ethn, name = "n_clients", sort = TRUE)
```

# 3. Clean Discharge Data

## 3.1 Remove Demo/Test Accounts

Same as demographics — filter out any rows where the provider or client ID contains "DEMO".

```{r demo-filter-discharge}
discharge_data_filtered <- remove_demo_rows(discharge_data, "Discharge")

# Expected to be FALSE — one client can have multiple assessment rows
cat("One row per client in discharge data:",
    n_distinct(discharge_data_filtered$client_system_id) == nrow(discharge_data_filtered), "\n")
```

## 3.2 Inspect Duplicate Client Records

Unlike demographics, it is expected for a client to appear more than once in the discharge report (e.g., multiple interventions or follow-ups). This chunk documents which columns vary across rows for the same client.

```{r discharge-duplicates}
discharge_data_filtered |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  filter(n > 1)

# Which fields differ across rows for the same client?
discharge_data_filtered |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  summarise(
    across(everything(), ~ {
      u <- unique(.x)
      if (length(u) > 1) paste(u, collapse = ", ") else NA_character_
    }),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  select(client_system_id, where(~ any(!is.na(.))))
```

## 3.3 Parse Pre/Post Measure Names

The `pre_measure_s` and `post_measure_s` fields combine the time point (e.g., "Initial", "Follow Up 1") and assessment name (e.g., "SDQ") into one string. We split these into separate columns so they can be matched and filtered independently.

Time points are matched case-insensitively and allow "Follow Up 1", "Follow-Up 1", "Followup 1", etc. They are standardized to "Initial" or "Follow Up N", and `post_follow_up_number` holds N as an integer.

A secondary trimmed name (first word only) is created because some providers abbreviate assessment names differently in the pre vs. post fields.

```{r parse-measure-names}
# Check raw values before parsing
unique(discharge_data_filtered$pre_measure_s)
unique(discharge_data_filtered$post_measure_s)
```

```{r clean-measure-names}
time_point_pattern <- regex("\\b(initial|follow[\\s-]*up\\s*\\d+)\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)

discharge_data_filtered <- discharge_data_filtered |>
  mutate(
    pre_time_point      = standardize_time_point(str_extract(pre_measure_s, time_point_pattern)),
    pre_assessment_name = str_squish(str_remove(pre_measure_s, time_point_pattern))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    post_time_point      = standardize_time_point(str_extract(post_measure_s, time_point_pattern)),
    post_assessment_name = str_squish(str_remove(post_measure_s, time_point_pattern))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Exact match check
    MatchDistinct = pre_assessment_name == post_assessment_name,
    # First-word match — handles cases where "SDQ" appears as "SDQ Strengths & Difficulties..."
    trimmed_pre_assessment_name  = word(pre_assessment_name, 1),
    trimmed_post_assessment_name = word(post_assessment_name, 1),
    trimmed_match = trimmed_pre_assessment_name == trimmed_post_assessment_name,
    # Follow-up number (NA when the post measure is not a follow-up)
    post_follow_up_number = as.integer(str_extract(post_time_point, "\\d+"))
  )

# Measure strings with no recognizable time point — review these
discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter((!is.na(pre_measure_s)  & is.na(pre_time_point)) |
         (!is.na(post_measure_s) & is.na(post_time_point))) |>
  count(pre_measure_s, post_measure_s, name = "n_rows")

# Rows where even the trimmed names don't match — review these manually
discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter(trimmed_match == FALSE)
```

## 3.4 Fix Missing Funding Rounds

Some providers did not select a funding round in eInsight ("No Funding Round Selected"). Based on program records, we manually assign the correct round for known providers.

| Provider ID | Organization                   | Correct Round |
|-------------|--------------------------------|---------------|
| 604         | Monterey Health Dept           | 2             |
| 508         | Children of the Rainbow        | 2             |
| 607         | Youth for Change               | 1             |
| 573         | Homeless Children's Network    | 2 (all rows; see Open Issues) |
| 709         | Placer County Office of Education | 1          |

```{r fix-funding-rounds}
# Recorded rounds for these providers before the fix
discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter(provider_id %in% c("604", "508", "607", "573", "709")) |>
  count(provider_id, funding_round_before_fix = funding_round)

discharge_data_filtered_clean <- discharge_data_filtered |>
  mutate(
    funding_round = case_when(
      provider_id == "604" & funding_round == "No Funding Round Selected" ~ "2",
      provider_id == "508" & funding_round == "No Funding Round Selected" ~ "2",
      provider_id == "607" & funding_round == "No Funding Round Selected" ~ "1",
      provider_id == "573"                                                 ~ "2",  # all rows (intentional?)
      provider_id == "709" & funding_round == "No Funding Round Selected" ~ "1",
      TRUE ~ funding_round
    )
  )

# Funding round values after the fix (check labels are consistent, e.g., "2" vs "Round 2")
discharge_data_filtered_clean |>
  count(funding_round)
```

# 4. EDA — Clients with Multiple Interventions

Some clients appear in the discharge data more than once because they participated in more than one intervention (or had multiple follow-up time points). Understanding this structure is important before analysis, because rows are not independent.

## 4.1 Identify Clients with >1 Complete Intervention

"Complete" here means the row has both a pre AND a post measure (i.e., the client has a pre–post pair, not just a baseline or a lone follow-up).

```{r dup-complete-interventions}
# Summarize what varies across rows for each client with >1 complete pair
dup_client_system_id <- discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter(!is.na(pre_measure_s) & !is.na(post_measure_s)) |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  summarise(
    across(everything(), ~ {
      u <- unique(.x)
      if (length(u) > 1) paste(u, collapse = ", ") else NA_character_
    }),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  select(client_system_id, where(~ any(!is.na(.))))

# Pull all rows for those clients
dup_clients <- discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter(
    client_system_id %in% dup_client_system_id$client_system_id,
    !is.na(pre_measure_s) & !is.na(post_measure_s)
  )

cat("Clients with >1 complete pre-post pair:", n_distinct(dup_clients$client_system_id), "\n")
```

## 4.2 Concurrent Interventions (Same Pre-Completion Date)

Clients who had two or more different assessments completed on the same date — indicating they were enrolled in multiple interventions simultaneously.

```{r dup-same-time}
dup_clients_same_time <- dup_clients |>
  group_by(client_system_id, pre_completion_date) |>
  summarise(
    across(pre_measure_s, ~ {
      u <- unique(.x)
      if (length(u) > 1) paste(u, collapse = ", ") else NA_character_
    }),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(pre_measure_s))

# Full rows for those clients
dup_clients_same_time_data <- discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter(client_system_id %in% dup_clients_same_time$client_system_id)

# One row per client x date, so count distinct clients
cat("Clients with concurrent interventions:", n_distinct(dup_clients_same_time$client_system_id), "\n")
```

## 4.3 Sequential Interventions (Different Start Dates)

Clients who completed interventions at genuinely different time points — i.e., they started a new intervention after finishing a prior one.

```{r dup-diff-time}
dup_clients_diff_time <- dup_clients |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  filter(n_distinct(intervention_start, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) |>
  summarise(
    n_intervention_start    = n_distinct(intervention_start, na.rm = TRUE),
    intervention_start_dates = paste(sort(unique(intervention_start)), collapse = ", "),
    pre_measure_s_values = {
      vals <- unique(na.omit(pre_measure_s))
      if (length(vals) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(vals, collapse = ", ")
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

dup_clients_diff_time_data <- discharge_data_filtered |>
  filter(client_system_id %in% dup_clients_diff_time$client_system_id)

cat("Clients with sequential interventions:", nrow(dup_clients_diff_time), "\n")
```

## 4.4 Reconcile the Categories

The concurrent and sequential groups do not add up to the total for three reasons: a client can be in both, the concurrent table had one row per client × date (now counted as distinct clients above), and some clients fit neither, most often because **one initial assessment is paired with more than one follow-up** (e.g., Initial→Follow Up 1 and Initial→Follow Up 2 are two complete pairs). The table below gives every client with more than one complete pair a set of flags so the groups can be counted without gaps or double counting.

```{r dup-reconcile}
concurrent_ids <- dup_clients |>
  group_by(client_system_id, pre_completion_date) |>
  filter(n_distinct(pre_measure_s) > 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(client_system_id) |>
  pull(client_system_id)

sequential_ids <- dup_clients_diff_time$client_system_id

multi_follow_up_ids <- dup_clients |>
  group_by(client_system_id, pre_measure_s, pre_completion_date) |>
  filter(n_distinct(post_measure_s) > 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(client_system_id) |>
  pull(client_system_id)

dup_client_types <- tibble(client_system_id = unique(dup_clients$client_system_id)) |>
  mutate(
    concurrent          = client_system_id %in% concurrent_ids,
    sequential          = client_system_id %in% sequential_ids,
    multiple_follow_ups = client_system_id %in% multi_follow_up_ids,
    none_of_these       = !(concurrent | sequential | multiple_follow_ups)
  )

# Every combination that occurs, with the number of clients in it
dup_client_types |>
  count(concurrent, sequential, multiple_follow_ups, none_of_these, name = "n_clients")
```

# 5. Join Demographic and Discharge Data

Left join from discharge data onto demographics so we retain all assessment rows. Clients without a demographics record will have `NA` in demographic columns but remain in the dataset. All four ID columns were converted to text when the files were read, and the join is checked to be many-to-one (each discharge row matches at most one demographic row).

```{r join-data}
no_demo_match <- anti_join(discharge_data_filtered_clean, demographic_data_filtered, by = id_cols)

cat("Discharge rows with no demographic match:      ", nrow(no_demo_match), "\n")
cat("  ...client_system_id is in demographics       \n")
cat("     (other IDs differ, e.g., provider):       ",
    sum(no_demo_match$client_system_id %in% demographic_data_filtered$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("  ...client was dropped as a demographic dup:  ",
    sum(no_demo_match$client_system_id %in% duplicates$client_system_id), "\n")

all_data <- left_join(
  discharge_data_filtered_clean,
  demographic_data_filtered,
  by = id_cols,
  relationship = "many-to-one"
)

# Columns present in both files (other than the join keys) get .x/.y suffixes
suffixed <- names(all_data)[str_detect(names(all_data), "\\.(x|y)$")]
if (length(suffixed) > 0) {
  warning("Columns duplicated by the join: ", paste(suffixed, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}
```

---

# 6. Quick Counts

```{r counts}
cat("Unique clients in demographics (served):      ", n_distinct(demographic_data_filtered$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("Unique clients in joined dataset (outcomes):  ", n_distinct(all_data$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("Rows in joined dataset:                       ", nrow(all_data), "\n")
cat("Joined rows with no demographic record:       ", nrow(no_demo_match), "\n")
```

---

# 7. Write Clean CSVs

```{r write-csvs}
write_csv(all_data,                      file.path(out_dir, "demographic_discharge_clean.csv"))
write_csv(demographic_data_filtered,     file.path(out_dir, "demographic_data_clean.csv"))
write_csv(discharge_data_filtered_clean, file.path(out_dir, "discharge_data_clean.csv"))

cat("CSVs written successfully.\n")
```
